title: Measurement of urinary leukocyte esterase activity: a screening test for urinary tract infections (Chernow et al., Ann Emerg Med. 1984;13(3):150-4)

claims.text: Leukocyte esterase is an enzyme released only from leukocytes, and testing for it in urine indicates the presence of pyuria.
claims.byte_quote: We evaluated the efficacy of testing for the presence of esterase (an enzyme released only from leukocytes) in the urine as an indicator of the presence of pyuria.

claims.text: A dipstick test for urinary leukocyte esterase activity was hypothesized to be a rapid, simple screening technique for detecting UTIs.
claims.byte_quote: We hypothesized that a "dipstick" test for urinary leukocyte esterase activity would be a rapid and simple screening technique for detecting urinary tract infections (UTI).

claims.text: Study population: 203 patients (148 outpatients, 55 inpatients) with suspected UTI.
claims.byte_quote: we collected fresh urine specimens from 203 patients (148 outpatients, 55 inpatients) with a suspected UTI.

claims.text: Significant bacteriuria was defined as >= 10^5 organisms/mL; 49 of 203 specimens met this threshold.
claims.byte_quote: Of the 203 specimens, 49 showed significant bacteriuria (greater than or equal to 10(5) organisms/mL).

claims.text: Leukocyte esterase dipstick was 100% sensitive (0% false negatives) and 76% specific (24% false positives) for predicting significant bacteriuria.
claims.byte_quote: The leukocyte esterase test was 100% sensitive (0% false negatives) with a 76% specificity (24% false positives) in predicting significant bacteriuria.

claims.text: Urinary nitrite testing was highly specific (99% specificity, 0.6% false positives) but insensitive (27% sensitivity, 73% false negatives).
claims.byte_quote: Although a positive nitrite reaction was more specific (99% specificity, 0.6% false positives), it was insensitive (27% sensitivity, 73% false negatives).
